desc:
Given a string s, return the lexicographically largest non-empty subsequence of s. A string is larger than another if at the first position where they differ it has the later letter, or if the other one is a proper prefix of it.

For example, for s = "abcab" the answer is "cb", for s = "zzaz" it is "zzz" and for s = "cba" it is "cba" itself.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: The first letter of the answer should be the biggest letter of the whole string. Which occurrence of it should you take?
Take every occurrence of the biggest letter: more copies make the answer longer, and a longer string beats its own prefix. Then repeat the idea on what is left after the last of them.
Walk from the right and keep a letter exactly when it is at least as large as every letter already kept (equivalently, every letter to its right).
editorial: The answer must start with the maximum letter m of s; any answer starting with something smaller loses immediately. Taking all occurrences of m is better than taking fewer, because a string with more trailing copies of the same letter is larger than its prefix. After the last occurrence of m, we repeat the same reasoning on the remaining suffix.

Putting it together, a letter belongs to the answer exactly when no letter strictly larger than it appears later in s. Scan from right to left, track the largest letter seen so far, keep the current letter if it is not smaller, then reverse the collected letters. O(n) time, O(n) space for the output.
